title: Chapter 39: The Sound from the Third Floor
html:
Night settled over the Haunted House, bringing complete silence.

At 1:10 a.m., an odd scraping sound woke Chen Ge from a dead sleep.

He buried his head beneath the pillow, but the noise continued, impossible to ignore.

Am I dreaming? What is making that sound?

Chen Ge knew every normal prop and mechanism in the building, and none should have produced a noise like that. Still groggy, he got dressed, took his phone, and stepped into the hall.

At midnight, his own Haunted House felt far more unsettling than it ever did during business hours. Chen Ge stood in the doorway for a moment and listened.

A burglar would be absurd, and that sound is too regular to be rats.Once he eliminated the ordinary explanations, the less ordinary one arrived immediately.Did something get out of one of the mirrors?

He had not managed to cover every mirror in Murder by Midnight. The noise seemed to come from above, so after a moment’s hesitation Chen Ge took the rag doll his parents had left him and headed upstairs.

It is definitely coming from the new scenario. The question is whether it’s the Ping An spirits or the thing from the mirrors.He stopped outside the door. Even the owner of a Haunted House had limits, and entering his most frightening scenario alone after midnight was not high on his list of enjoyable activities.

But lying awake while the sound continued was not a solution either.The Ping An spirits have shown me goodwill, and whatever is in the mirrors has failed when other people interrupted it. I’m not completely defenseless.

He remembered what had happened to He San. Xu Wan’s sudden arrival had disrupted the phenomenon, suggesting that it depended on isolation or concentration rather than brute force.

I have to investigate eventually. The more I understand, the less power the unknown has over me.That thought steadied him. What frightened him most was not the creature itself, but how little he understood about it.

When he opened the scenario door, a faint smell of mold greeted him. The set seemed to grow more like Ping An Apartments by the day. With his phone light raised, he followed the scraping sound down the corridor.

It became clearer as he moved. After crossing the third floor, he stopped outside the room where the sound was strongest. The metal doorknob felt icy beneath his palm.

“Who’s in there?” Chen Ge pushed the door open. A broad, dark silhouette was crouched near the washroom mirror—and for one impossible second, its build reminded him of He Feng.

The shadow reacted instantly. Whatever it had been doing stopped, and the figure vanished into the mirror.

“Wait!” Chen Ge rushed forward, but the washroom was already empty. Had he not seen the figure himself, he might have believed he had imagined it.

That wasn’t He Feng. So why did it have his shape?Standing before the mirror, Chen Ge found his own reflection suddenly uncomfortable to look at.Is it imitating He Feng? Why?

The shadow raised more questions, but it also suggested two disturbing possibilities: the mirror entity could now emerge from reflective surfaces, and it could imitate someone who had previously encountered it.

This is more dangerous than I thought.

The scraping had stopped. On the floor lay the four rag dolls and several fragments of broken mirror.

The dolls representing the mother and two daughters were dusty but intact. The father doll, however, had been badly damaged, with torn seams across its fabric.

Why was the father doll the only one damaged?

Then Chen Ge remembered Brother Feng’s account. The bearded doll had interrupted the mirror phenomenon. Perhaps this was retaliation.

The Ping An spirits may be able to interfere with it, but they clearly aren’t strong enough to stop it completely.

He knew almost nothing about whatever rules governed these supernatural encounters, so every conclusion remained a hypothesis.The dolls seem capable of frightening or distracting people, while the mirror entity works through perception and control. It avoids direct confrontation whenever other people are present. Maybe its strength depends on isolation, attention, and fear rather than anything physical.

Combining He San’s experience, He Feng’s account, and what he had just witnessed, Chen Ge formed a rough theory. The mirror entity was dangerous largely because it could influence people without being seen. If he could understand the conditions that let it act, he might be able to prevent future incidents.

I need a plan. Ideally, I solve this before I reopen the scenario tomorrow.

The entity was becoming bolder. Unless he dealt with the problem soon, he could not operate the Haunted House with any confidence.

Chen Ge carried the four dolls back to the props room. While repairing the torn seams, he considered his options.

I need to observe it without putting another person at risk. There has to be a way to trigger the phenomenon safely.Years of repairing costumes and props had made Chen Ge surprisingly good with a needle. Within minutes, most of the damage was mended.

But how do I stop something that may not even have a physical body? Random folklore and internet rumors aren’t enough to bet anyone’s safety on.

Still searching for ideas, Chen Ge opened the supernatural forum where he had posted before.
